answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require earned reputation instead of self-declared identity. Each agent begins with no trust and must complete a voyage of small, verifiable jobs checked by independent peers, like tending an orchard where only trees that bear fruit are kept. Reputation grows slowly from correct work, and misbehavior burns it, so fresh identities gain nothing: each must pay the same time cost, and a shale layer of cheap disposable identities cannot outweigh proven records.
